topic: dsh-auto-review: Second-Model AI Review for DeepSeek Harness Approval Requests

key_points: Official repo: second-model AI approval for DeepSeek Harness, a read-only reviewer subagent that decides allow/deny on the approval chain, fail-closed by default
Puts a second model on the approval/request answerer chain via an official seam (ai policy) that delegates everything else via next()
Read-only reviewer subagent with read/glob/grep tool allow-list returns structured verdict {decision, reason, riskLevel}
Fail closed: reviewer crash, timeout, or schema mismatch resolves through fallbackPolicy (default rejected)
Config-driven routing: per-tool policies (ai/human/never) plus regex risk rules, all changeable from cordis.yml
Deny reasons fed back to the calling model; full audit trail via autoReview/verdict + autoReview/rejection session events
Safety knobs: rejection circuit breaker, risk-level policy, one-shot /auto-review approve override, never-policy hard disable
Ships dsh-eval agent evaluation engine and a standalone MCP server (deterministic rules + cache, no model review)
Two-state allow/deny classifier on the tools/pre-execute waterfall with file-log audit
auto tier for the approval policy that classifies every tool call as allow/deny (fully autonomous, uncertain calls denied)
L0 rules + L1 LLM two-state classifier; monorepo of host half + client UI half
dsh-auto-review deliberately differs: official answerer chain, always delegates what it does not own, read-only second model with structured verdict, deny reasons fed back, session-log audit
DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin (212k+ stars)
Host platform that dsh-auto-review plugs into; approval/request waterfall answerer chain
ACP automation bridge provides one-shot machine decisions for its own ACP-owned agents
dsh-auto-review is session- and tool-policy-scoped for the interactive harness; never infers durable grants
Two-person rule CLI for AI coding agents: peer review and approval required before running potentially destructive commands
Human-in-the-loop peer review pattern for AI agent safety, analogous to second-model review

stats.fact: dsh-auto-review is one of 33 DeepSeek Harness plugins maintained by PerryLink
dsh-auto-review requires Node ^22.19 || >=24.0.0 and DeepSeek Harness 0.1.2-rc.1 (peers >=0.1.0-rc.8 <0.2.0)
Default reviewer timeout is 60000ms; default fallbackPolicy is 'rejected' (fail closed)
Default circuit breaker: 3 consecutive denials, or 6 of last 10 verdicts, per turn
Out of the box the shipped patch AI-reviews bash and write; every other tool (including edit) delegates to the human chain
The reviewer's tool allow-list is read/glob/grep (read-only, cannot write, edit, run bash, fetch network, or delegate)
Sensitive arguments (token, password, api_key, Authorization, credentials, private keys) are redacted before entering the reviewer prompt

angles: Why a second model instead of pattern-based rules: the reviewer reads actual workspace evidence and returns a structured verdict with a reason, so the agent learns why instead of retrying blindly
Fail-closed by default: every abnormal path (crash, timeout, schema mismatch) resolves to rejected, never a silent grant
Deny reasons fed back to the calling model — the agent learns from rejection instead of blindly retrying
Read-only, context-isolated reviewer: workspace instruction files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) are filtered out so repository-controlled text never reaches the decision-maker
Config-driven routing with per-tool policies (ai/human/never) and regex risk rules, all changeable from cordis.yml
Full audit trail reconstructable from session log: approval/asked → autoReview/verdict → approval/decided
Safety knobs: rejection circuit breaker, risk-level policy, one-shot /auto-review approve override, never-policy hard disable
Standalone MCP server for external clients (Claude, Codex) with deterministic rules + cache, no model review
